about: cesr.parse cases for count-code framing in genus 2.00. Each asserts the offset at which every group ends, so a parser that reads a size as a number of items rather than quadlets (triplets in the binary domain) ends a group in the wrong place even if it reports the size digits correctly.

cases.title: A group's size counts quadlets, not primitives
cases.description: The founding case of the suite. A -J group holds two primitives, a D key (11 quadlets) and a 0B signature (22 quadlets), so its size is 33, not 2. A second -J group follows it. A parser that counts items reads 33 as 33 primitives and cannot find the second group where it starts. The symbol legends of the Encoding Scheme Symbols Table and the indexed-code symbol table say a count code's digits determine 'the count of the following Primitives or groups of Primitives'; this case rests on the explicit rule at the Count Code tables section instead, and the conflict between the two texts is noted, not resolved, here.

cases.title: A controller signature group's size counts quadlets, not signatures
cases.description: An attachments group (-C) holds a controller indexed signature group (-K) of three Ed25519 indexed signatures. -K has size 66 (3 x 22 quadlets), not 3; -C has size 67. A digest group follows. This is the framing that made streams unreadable between keripy and the item-counting implementations. The symbol legends of the Encoding Scheme Symbols Table and the indexed-code symbol table say a count code's digits determine 'the count of the following Primitives or groups of Primitives'; this case rests on the explicit rule at the Count Code tables section instead, and the conflict between the two texts is noted, not resolved, here.

cases.title: In the binary domain a group's size counts triplets, not primitives
cases.description: The stream of CESR-0025 in the binary domain. The size digits are unchanged (33) and now count 3-byte triplets, so the first group ends 99 bytes after its count code. The symbol legends of the Encoding Scheme Symbols Table and the indexed-code symbol table say a count code's digits determine 'the count of the following Primitives or groups of Primitives'; this case rests on the explicit rule at the Count Code tables section instead, and the conflict between the two texts is noted, not resolved, here.

cases.title: Parse a large (eight-character) count code
cases.description: --J is the large form of the generic list code: two selector characters, the type, and five size digits. Here it frames one D key, size 11, written --JAAAAL.

cases.title: A nested group's quadlets count toward its enclosing group
cases.description: A -J group holds a D key, a nested -J group (holding an E digest and a 0B signature, size 33) and an M short number. The outer size, 46, counts the nested group's count code and contents as well as the other primitives.

cases.title: Switch between the text and binary domains at group boundaries
cases.description: A text -J group, then a binary -J group, then a text -J group. Each group's count code is the first thing at its boundary, so its first tritet (0b001 for text '-', 0b111 for binary) tells the parser which domain the group is in.

cases.title: An empty group has size zero and ends at its count code
cases.description: A -J group of size 0 followed immediately by a -J group holding one D key. The empty group ends where its count code ends.
